name: Spanish Paella Valenciana
description: Real paella Valenciana is a dry rice dish, not a risotto or pilaf, and the real, defining technique is to never stir the rice once it's spread evenly in the pan - stirring releases starch and turns it to mush. Real socarrat, the prized crispy bottom layer, comes from raising the heat at the very end until you actually hear a crackling sound; the seafood-and-chorizo version many people know outside Spain is a real, later adaptation, not the traditional recipe, which is built on chicken, green beans, and butter beans.
steps_detailed: Soak the saffron in a tablespoon of warm broth for 10 minutes.
Brown the chicken in the olive oil in a wide, shallow pan, 6-7 minutes, then push to the side.
Add the green beans and butter beans, and cook 3-4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and paprika, and cook 2-3 minutes into a real sofrito base.
Add the broth and saffron with its soaking liquid, and bring to a boil.
Scatter the rice evenly over the whole pan and distribute with a spatula - then do not stir again for the rest of cooking, real technique depends on this.
Simmer 15-18 minutes without stirring, until the liquid is absorbed.
Raise the heat for the final 1-2 minutes, listening for a real crackling sound at the bottom, which signals the socarrat has formed.

name: Spanish Tortilla Española
description: Tortilla española, a real potato and egg dish, depends on real technique cooking the potato and onion slowly in olive oil until genuinely soft (not crisp), which is what gives the tortilla its distinctive creamy interior once combined with the eggs.
steps_detailed: Cook the potato and onion slowly in the olive oil over low heat, 20-22 minutes, until genuinely soft, not crisp.
Drain, reserving the oil, and let cool slightly.
Beat the eggs and mix in the potato and onion.
Heat a little of the reserved oil in a small pan, pour in the mixture, and cook 4-5 minutes until mostly set.
Flip carefully (using a plate) and cook 2-3 minutes more until just set through.

name: Spanish Gazpacho
description: Gazpacho, a real cold tomato soup, is a beloved Spanish summer staple, real technique blending everything raw and chilling thoroughly, never cooking it.
steps_detailed: Blend everything together until completely smooth.
Chill at least 1 hour before serving cold.

name: Spanish Patatas Bravas
description: Patatas bravas, crispy fried potatoes with a real spicy tomato sauce, is a beloved Spanish tapas staple, real technique double-frying the potatoes for real extra crispiness.
steps_detailed: Fry the potato at a lower temperature, 325F (163C), for 5-6 minutes, until soft but pale. Remove and rest 10 minutes.
Simmer the tomatoes, jalapeño, and paprika together 12-15 minutes into a spicy sauce.
Fry the potato a second time at 375F (190C) for 3-4 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.
Serve the potatoes topped with the sauce.

name: Spanish Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and olive oil, reflecting Spain's extensive Mediterranean and Atlantic coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and olive oil, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Spanish Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Spain, especially in Andalusia.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Spanish Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Spanish home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

name: Spanish Alioli
description: Alioli, a real garlic-forward emulsified sauce, is a beloved Spanish condiment, real technique whisking the garlic and oil together slowly to build a genuine emulsion.
steps_detailed: Whisk the garlic into the mayonnaise until well combined.
